examples.ko: 동생이 내 새 가방을 자꾸 탐내요.
examples.en: My younger sibling keeps coveting my new bag.

examples.ko: 그는 사장 자리를 탐내서 몰래 준비했어요.
examples.en: He coveted the boss's seat and prepared in secret.
You must not covet other people's things.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 우승을 탐냈지만 아쉽게 졌어요.
examples.en: That player wanted the title badly but sadly lost.
It's a position everyone wants, so competition is fierce.

examples.ko: 친구의 재능을 탐내지 말고 제 길을 가세요.
examples.en: Don't covet your friend's talent, just follow your own path.

explain: '남의 물건을 탐내다'처럼 대상을 목적어로 써요. 갖고 싶은 마음이 크고 욕심 같은 느낌이 있어서 좋은 뜻은 아니에요. 단순히 갖고 싶으면 '갖고 싶어 하다', 부러운 마음이면 '부러워하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Don't covet other people's things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하지 말라고 부드럽게 말릴 때 쓰는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to tell someone not to do it.

phrases.example: 저도 어릴 때 형의 장난감을 탐냈어요.
phrases.en: I also coveted my older brother's toys when I was little.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 갖고 싶어 욕심을 냈다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense: I wanted it greedily in the past.

phrases.en: Many people covet that position.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙이면 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-는' lets it describe the noun that follows.

explain_en: Spoken, common: wanting something someone else has, like a kid with a toy. The target is the object, as in 남의 물건을 탐내다. It carries a sense of greed, so it isn't a compliment. For simply wanting something, use 갖고 싶어 하다, and for envy use 부러워하다.

t90.ax: You must not covet other people's things.

en: to be unreliable; to be groundless

examples.ko: 몇 년 준비한 일이 하루 만에 끝나서 너무 허망해요.
examples.en: Something I prepared for years ended in a day, and it feels so empty.

examples.ko: 열심히 모은 돈을 사기로 잃고 나니 허망했어요.
examples.en: After losing the money I worked hard to save to a scam, I felt hollow.

examples.ko: 허망한 마음에 한참 동안 하늘만 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: Feeling empty, I just stared at the sky for a long time.

examples.ko: 인생이 허망하다는 생각이 들 때가 있어요.
examples.en: There are times when I feel that life is futile.

examples.ko: 그렇게 허망하게 지는 경기는 처음 봤어요.
examples.en: I've never seen a game lost so abruptly and pointlessly.

examples.ko: 너무 허망해서 아무 말도 나오지 않았어요.
examples.en: I felt so empty that I couldn't say a word.

explain: '허무하다'와 비슷하지만, '허망하다'는 기대하거나 애쓴 일이 갑자기 헛되게 끝났을 때 더 잘 어울려요. '허망하게 끝나다/지다'처럼 '허망하게' 형태로도 써요.

phrases.en: His dream vanished in vain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대와 달리 헛되게 끝났음을 말하는 부사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adverb form meaning something ended in vain, against expectations.

phrases.example: 큰 일이 끝나고 나자 허망한 기분이 들었어요.
phrases.en: After the big task ended, I felt a sense of emptiness.
phrases.nuance_ko: '허망하다'를 '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔 명사 앞에서 그 감정을 꾸며 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, describing the feeling before a noun.

phrases.en: The game ended so early that I felt empty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이지만 갑자기 헛되게 끝난 느낌은 '허망하다'가 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word, but 'heomanghada' stresses a sudden, futile ending more.

explain_en: It is similar to '허무하다', but '허망하다' fits best when something you hoped for or worked on ends suddenly in vain. It is also used in the form '허망하게', as in '허망하게 끝나다/지다'.

en: to confuse; to muddle; to mix up

examples.en: I sometimes mix up 'left' and 'right.'
You must not confuse public and private matters.

examples.ko: 두 사람을 혼동해서 이름을 잘못 불렀어요.
examples.en: I confused the two people and called the wrong name.
Because I mixed up the dates, I missed the appointment.

examples.ko: 소금과 설탕을 혼동하지 않게 이름을 써 두었어요.
examples.en: I wrote labels so I wouldn't confuse salt and sugar.
Many people confuse the twin brothers.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '헷갈리다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '혼동하다'는 두 가지를 같은 것으로 잘못 보는 상황을 설명할 때 써요. '~와 ~를 혼동하다'처럼 두 대상을 함께 말해요. 반대로 나누어 알아보는 것은 '구별하다'예요.

phrases.en: Please don't mix up the two words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설명이나 안내에서 헷갈리지 말라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in explanations or notices to ask people not to mix things up.

phrases.example: 저는 이 두 글자가 자꾸 헷갈려요.
phrases.en: I keep getting these two letters mixed up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혼동하다'보다 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는, 같은 뜻의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more common everyday word with a similar meaning.

phrases.en: '다르다' and '틀리다' are easy to mix up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-기 쉽다'를 붙여 잘 헷갈리는 것을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-기 쉽다' says something is easy to mix up.

explain_en: Mistake one thing for another; confuse similar items. In daily talk 헷갈리다 is used more, while 혼동하다 is for explaining that two things are wrongly taken as the same. It takes both objects, as in ~와 ~를 혼동하다. The opposite, telling them apart, is 구별하다.

en: to be unclear; to be blurred; to be hazy

examples.en: I couldn't sleep, so my eyes look dull and unfocused.
I went into the meeting in a foggy state of mind.
He ended up giving a vague answer.
After taking the medicine, my head became foggy.
His attitude is so unclear that I don't know what he means.
That person's explanation stayed vague to the very end.

explain: 정신, 눈빛, 기억, 태도가 또렷하지 않을 때 써요. '흐리다'가 날씨나 유리에도 쓰이는 것과 달리, 이 말은 주로 사람의 상태나 태도에 써요.

phrases.en: I got on the bus with dull, sleepy eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 '눈'을 꾸며 초점 없고 또렷하지 않은 눈빛을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form modifies 'eyes' to describe a dull, unfocused look.

phrases.en: It was a long time ago, so my memory is hazy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기억이 또렷하지 않을 때 해요체로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite form used when a memory isn't clear.

phrases.en: I took cold medicine, and now my mind feels foggy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리가 맑지 않고 멍한 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when your mind feels foggy and not clear.

explain_en: Hazy — mind or sight is foggy, dull, or not sharp (정신이 흐리멍덩하다) It is used when someone's mind, gaze, memory or attitude is not sharp or clear. Unlike '흐리다', which also fits weather or glass, this word mostly describes a person's state or attitude.

en: to be excited; to feel thrilled; to get worked up

examples.en: I'm so excited about going on a trip tomorrow.
I got more excited as the final approached.
He delivered the news in an excited voice.

examples.ko: 너무 흥분되어서 밤에 잠이 안 왔어요.
examples.en: I was so excited that I couldn't sleep at night.
I took a deep breath to calm my excited heart.

examples.ko: 흥분될 때는 천천히 말하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: When you're worked up, it's good to speak slowly.

explain: '신나다', '설레다'는 기분 좋은 설렘이고, '흥분되다'는 기쁨뿐 아니라 화가 났을 때도 몸과 마음이 달아오르는 느낌이에요. 그래서 문맥을 보고 좋은 흥분인지 나쁜 흥분인지 알아야 해요.

phrases.en: I'm so excited that I can't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말하는 연결형이에요. 뒤에 몸이나 행동의 결과가 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form giving a reason, followed by a physical or behavioral result.

phrases.example: 너무 흥분하지 말고 천천히 말해 봐요.
phrases.en: Don't get so worked up; speak slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흥분되다'는 저절로 느끼는 상태이고, '흥분하다'는 사람이 그렇게 행동하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 흥분되다 is a state you feel; 흥분하다 describes a person acting excited.

phrases.en: Tomorrow is the picnic, so I'm all fluttery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기분 좋은 기대를 말할 때 더 알맞은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A better fit for pleasant anticipation.
phrases.en_equiv: to feel a flutter of excitement

explain_en: Passive; excitement comes over you, spoken. '신나다' and '설레다' are happy excitement; '흥분되다' is being worked up in body and mind, which can come from joy or from anger. Context tells you which.

dis.h: feel thrilled; a feeling comes over you
gh: get worked up, even angry; active

p.n: 흥분하다 is more active; 흥분되다 is the feeling itself.

t90.ax: He delivered the news in an excited voice.

examples.en: My father tills the field with a hoe.
I went out to the garden plot carrying a hoe.

examples.ko: 괭이가 무뎌서 흙이 잘 안 파져요.
examples.en: The hoe is dull, so the soil doesn't dig well.
I washed the soil off the hoe with water.
The hoe handle broke, so I bought a new one.

examples.ko: 이 괭이는 날이 넓어서 쓰기 편해요.
examples.en: This hoe has a wide blade, so it's easy to use.

explain: 밭을 파고 일구는 농기구예요. 작은 '호미'는 쪼그려 앉아 잡초를 매는 데 쓰고, 괭이는 서서 흙을 크게 파는 데 써서 쓰임이 달라요. 도시에서는 텃밭이나 농촌 이야기에서 만나는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I've been hoeing since morning, so my arms hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 괭이로 땅을 파는 일을 하나의 행동처럼 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the act of digging the ground with a hoe.

phrases.en: I dug the ground with a hoe and planted potatoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 괭이를 도구로 쓰는 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic use of a hoe as a tool.
phrases.en_equiv: to dig the ground with a hoe

phrases.en: I left the hoe and the shovel in the shed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밭일에 같이 쓰는 도구와 함께 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often said together with other tools used in farm work.

explain_en: Larger long-handled hoe for breaking up and turning soil. It is a farm tool used to dig and break up soil. A small '호미' is used while squatting to weed, whereas a 괭이 is used standing to dig soil in bigger strokes. In cities you mostly meet the word in talk about garden plots or the countryside.

t90.ax: My father tills the field with a hoe.

en: to be squalid; to be shabby; to be filthy

examples.en: It's a humble place, but please sit comfortably.
The room was shabby, but it was a home with a warm heart.

examples.ko: 누추하게 사는 것 같아도 늘 깨끗하게 청소해요.
examples.en: It may look like a shabby life, but I always clean thoroughly.
It's an old inn, so it looks shabby from the outside.

examples.ko: 이사 간 집이 너무 누추해서 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: The house we moved into was so shabby that it hurt me.

examples.ko: 누추하다고 생각했는데 막상 들어가 보니 아늑했어요.
examples.en: I thought it would be shabby, but once I went in, it was cozy.

explain: 손님을 부를 때 '누추한 곳에 오셨네요'처럼 자기 집을 낮춰서 말하는 인사로도 써요. 남의 집이나 사람에게 직접 쓰면 실례가 돼요. '허름하다'가 낡은 느낌이라면 이 말은 초라하고 지저분한 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.example: 누추한 곳에 이렇게 와 주셔서 감사해요.
phrases.en: Thank you for coming to this humble place.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손님에게 자기 집을 낮춰 말하는 인사로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to humbly describe your own home when welcoming a guest.

phrases.en: It's an old building, so the inside looks shabby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보기에 초라하고 낡았다고 느낄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something looks shabby and worn.

phrases.en: His clothes are shabby, but he is a warm-hearted person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낡고 초라한 옷을 입은 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone wearing worn, shabby clothes.

explain_en: It is also used as a humble greeting when you invite a guest and run down your own home, as in '누추한 곳에 오셨네요'. Using it directly about someone else's home or person is rude. While '허름하다' just feels old, this word feels more poor and dirty.

examples.en: My grandmother lives in a one-story house with a yard.
A one-story house has no stairs, so it's comfortable to live in.

examples.ko: 시골에서 작은 단층집을 한 채 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a small one-story house in the countryside.
Most houses in this neighborhood are one-story.
Since it's a one-story house, I don't worry about noise from upstairs.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 살던 단층집이 아직도 생각나요.
examples.en: I still remember the one-story house I lived in as a child.

explain: '이층집'과 대비되는 말이에요. 아파트나 빌라와 달리 한 층으로 된 개인 주택을 떠올리는 말이고, '단층 주택'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I lived in a single-story house when I was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 층으로 된 집에 산다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you live in a one-floor house.
phrases.en_equiv: to live in a one-story house

phrases.en: There are many single-story houses in this neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: '단층집'과 같은 뜻이고 조금 더 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '단층집', a bit more formal.

phrases.en: Which do you like better, a two-story house or a one-story house?
phrases.nuance_ko: 층수가 다른 집을 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to compare houses with different numbers of floors.

explain_en: It contrasts with '이층집' (a two-story house). It brings to mind a one-floor private home, unlike an apartment or villa, and it can also be called '단층 주택'.

examples.en: I filled a basin with water and washed my hands.

examples.ko: 빨래를 큰 대야에서 발로 밟아 빨았어요.
examples.en: I washed the laundry in a big basin by stepping on it.
It's handy to have a small basin.

examples.ko: 물이 넘치지 않게 대야를 조심히 들었어요.
examples.en: I carried the basin carefully so the water wouldn't spill.

examples.ko: 비가 새서 방 안에 대야로 물을 받았어요.
examples.en: The roof leaked, so I caught the water in a basin inside the room.
This basin is plastic, so it's light.

explain: '세숫대야'처럼 앞에 용도를 붙여 말하는 일이 많아요. 부엌에서 음식을 섞을 때는 '양푼'이나 '볼'을 쓰고, 씻거나 빨래할 때는 '대야'를 써요. 요즘은 수도에서 바로 씻어서 예전만큼 자주 보이지 않아요.

phrases.en: I filled the washbasin with warm water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼굴이나 손을 씻는 용도라는 걸 분명히 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear it is the basin used for washing face or hands.

phrases.en: I put water in the basin and washed my feet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이나 물건을 그릇에 넣는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes putting water or things into the basin.

phrases.en: Please lend me a basin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개수를 셀 때 '하나, 두 개'처럼 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Count it with '하나, 두 개' and so on.

explain_en: People often add the purpose in front, as in '세숫대야' (face-washing basin). In the kitchen, a mixing bowl is '양푼' or '볼', while '대야' is for washing and laundry. Because people now wash straight at the tap, you see it less than before.

t90.ax: It's handy to have a small basin.

en: to be faded; to lose color

examples.ko: 오래된 사진이 빛바래서 얼굴이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The old photo has faded, so I can't see the faces well.

examples.ko: 할머니 방에는 빛바랜 가족사진이 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: A faded family photo hangs in my grandmother's room.
The curtains have faded in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 빛바랜 청바지를 일부러 사는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people buy faded jeans on purpose.
Even if the book cover fades, the contents stay the same.
This letter has faded, but it is precious to me.

explain: 오래돼서 색이 옅어진 사진, 종이, 옷에 써요. '빛바랜 사진'처럼 '-ㄴ' 형태로 가장 자주 들어요. 추억이나 명성이 희미해졌다는 비유로도 쓰는데, 이때는 글에서 더 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: It's a faded piece of clothing, but still wearable.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 명사 앞에 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -ㄴ form before a noun is most common.

phrases.en: The cover of the old book has faded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 과거형으로 변한 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite past form describing something that has changed.

phrases.en: The curtain's color faded in the sun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 일상에서 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning and easy to use in daily speech.

explain_en: It is used for photos, paper and clothes whose color has become pale with age. You will most often hear the '-ㄴ' form, as in '빛바랜 사진'. It can also be used figuratively for memories or fame that have faded, mostly in writing.

examples.en: Water is leaking from the joint of the water pipe.

examples.ko: 이음매가 거의 안 보이게 벽지를 붙였어요.
examples.en: I put up the wallpaper so the seam is almost invisible.

examples.ko: 바닥 이음매 사이에 먼지가 잘 껴요.
examples.en: Dust easily gets stuck between the joints in the floor.
I filled the joint between the two boards with glue.
Please check whether the joint is sturdy.

examples.ko: 철로 이음매 부분에서 덜컹 소리가 나요.
examples.en: There's a clunking sound at the joint of the railway track.

explain: 물건과 물건이 이어지는 자리를 말해요. 옷감을 바느질해 이은 선은 보통 '솔기'라고 하고, 파이프, 벽지, 바닥처럼 이어 붙인 곳에는 '이음매'를 써요. 비유로 서로 연결되는 부분을 말할 때도 있어요.

phrases.en: The joints in the floor came apart, so I called for a repair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙여 놓은 자리가 틈이 생겨 떨어질 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for when a joined spot opens up or comes apart.

phrases.en: I filled the gap in the seam with silicone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이어 붙인 자리의 틈을 막는 수리 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in repair situations where you seal a gap in a joined spot.

phrases.en: Put tape on the seam area.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이음매' 뒤에 '부분'을 붙여 이어진 곳 근처를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 부분 points to the area around the joint.

explain_en: Where two objects join, like furniture or pipes. It refers to the spot where two things are joined. The stitched line in fabric is usually called '솔기', while '이음매' is used for pipes, wallpaper, floors and other joined parts. It can also be used figuratively for a connecting point.

t90.ax: Please check whether the joint is sturdy.

examples.en: Electric current is flowing through the wire, so don't touch it.

examples.ko: 전류가 너무 세면 기계가 고장 나요.
examples.en: If the current is too strong, the machine breaks.
In the experiment, I measured the strength of the current.
It's dangerous if electric current passes through your body.
The current from the battery lights up the bulb.
To cut off the current, switch off the power first.

explain: 전류는 전기가 도선을 따라 흐르는 흐름이에요. 학교 과학이나 안전 이야기에서 '전류가 흐르다', '전류가 세다'처럼 써요. 전기를 일으키는 힘인 '전압'과, 전기 자체를 가리키는 '전기'와 구별해서 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: Electric current is flowing through this wire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전류와 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb paired with 전류.

phrases.en: If the current is strong it is dangerous, so be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전류의 크기가 클 때 '세다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 세다 when the current is large.

phrases.en: Copper conducts electric current well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전류가 물체를 지나갈 수 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when current can pass through a material.

explain_en: Physics term: flow of electricity in a wire (전류가 흐르다) 전류 is the flow of electricity along a wire. You see it in school science and safety talk, as in '전류가 흐르다' and '전류가 세다'. Keep it separate from '전압' (voltage) and '전기' (electricity itself).

examples.en: There are many small gears inside a watch.
I observed the gears turning as they meshed.
I oiled the bicycle's gear.

examples.ko: 톱니바퀴 하나가 고장 나면 전체가 멈춰요.
examples.en: If one gear breaks, the whole thing stops.
I'm a part of the big cogwheel called the company.
The child eagerly assembled a gear toy.

explain: 기계 부품을 말하지만 큰 조직 안에서 맡은 일만 반복하는 사람을 비유할 때도 자주 써요. 외래어 '기어'는 자동차나 자전거의 속도 조절 장치를 말할 때 더 흔해요.

phrases.example: 두 부서의 일이 톱니바퀴처럼 맞물려 돌아가요.
phrases.en: mesh like gears
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이나 일이 빈틈없이 이어져 잘 돌아간다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes people or tasks fitting together smoothly with no gaps.

explain_en: It names a machine part, but is also used figuratively for a person who just repeats their role inside a big organization. The loanword 기어 is more common for the speed gears of cars and bikes.

examples.en: This chair has armrests, so it's comfortable.

examples.ko: 비행기 팔걸이는 옆 사람과 같이 쓰는 거예요.
examples.en: The airplane armrest is shared with the person next to you.
I watched the movie with my arm on the armrest.

examples.ko: 소파 팔걸이가 낡아서 천을 새로 씌웠어요.
examples.en: The sofa armrest was worn out, so I put new fabric on it.

examples.ko: 팔걸이를 올리면 침대처럼 누울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you lift the armrest, you can lie down like on a bed.

examples.ko: 팔걸이 없는 의자가 더 가볍고 싸요.
examples.en: Chairs without armrests are lighter and cheaper.

explain: 의자, 소파, 자동차 좌석 옆에서 팔을 올려놓는 부분이에요. 비행기나 영화관 좌석에서는 옆 사람과 같이 쓰기도 해요. 보통 '팔걸이가 있다/없다'로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I rested with my arms on the chair's armrests.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팔걸이를 쓰는 가장 기본적인 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to use an armrest.
phrases.en_equiv: to rest one's arm on the armrest

phrases.example: 이 소파는 팔걸이가 없어서 조금 불편해요.
phrases.en: This sofa has no armrests, so it is a bit uncomfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: '있다'의 반대 쓰임이에요. 가구를 고를 때 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '있다'. Often said when choosing furniture.

phrases.en: Grandfather sits in an armchair and reads the newspaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팔걸이가 있는 의자를 말해요. 한 단어로 붙여 쓰기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A chair with armrests. Often written as one word.

explain_en: It is the part beside a chair, sofa or car seat where you rest your arm. On planes or in cinemas you may share it with the person next to you. You often say '팔걸이가 있다/없다'.
